subject: Solstice Labs — post-call recap & technical deep-dive ask

Date: Tue, 18 Jun 2024 15:07:00 -0700
Subject: Solstice follow-up — recap, goals, and next steps

Hi Daniel / Priya — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and the asks we agreed to: 

1) Key pain 
- Current in-house serving is inconsistent at 99th percentile for conversational assistant (100–2200ms observed spikes). This leads to timeouts for internal customer flows.

2) Primary goals for a PoC
- Achieve 99th percentile tail latency <350ms for single-turn generation at 256 tokens
- Sustain 200 QPS for embedding-based search and 40 QPS for generation during peak load
- Keep expected per-token unit cost <= $0.0008 (target to meet budget)

3) Model + data constraints
- Production model: 7B-13B open model family, requirement for on-prem variant (VPC) during evaluation
- KV cache retention per session ~4–8k tokens; many sessions have long context windows (up to 6k tokens)

4) Topology preference
- Prefer single-region private deployment (VPC) with dedicated capacity for initial PoC; fall back to hosted if networking/mgmt overhead is prohibitive

5) Next steps (owners)
- Neha: share post-call notes and MPA/POC mutual action plan (attached) — today
- Karthik: share preliminary topology options and rough capacity sizing — EOD tomorrow
- Solstice: share sample QPS/traffic traces + any existing load test reports — by Friday

Attachments: solstice-postcall-notes.pdf, solstice-mop-draft.docx

Happy to jump back on a short call to align on the PoC success criteria. Proposed 30-min slot Thurs 10–11am PT if that works.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor

Subject: Re: Solstice follow-up — recap, goals, and next steps

Neha — thanks for the crisp recap. A few clarifications and requests from our side: 

- Latency target: 99th <350ms sounds right. We do have multi-turn flows where average response length is ~120 tokens but some longer generations hit ~400 tokens; can you confirm your PoC sizing handles 256–512 token tails?

- Throughput: 200 QPS for embeddings is peak for our search layer (mostly async). For generator QPS, 40 is average peak — but we need graceful degradation to lower-quality model under extreme load, not full failure.

- Model family: we prefer a GGML-quantized 13B if performance allows. Is Redwood able to support quantized variants and automatic fallback to smaller model variants for capacity bursts?

- Data controls: audit logs and KMS for key material are mandatory for our security team. We'll request SOC 2 evidence as part of procurement.

Action items from us:
- Priya will export one week of anonymized traffic traces and send them over by Friday (we'll include a sample session with 6k context).
- I'll send our procurement template and baseline security questionnaire (expecting some redlines).

Would like Karthik to comment on support for quantized 13B models and an initial topology (dedicated GPUs vs multi-node smaller instances).

Best,
Daniel

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Solstice follow-up — recap, goals, and next steps (technical notes)

Neha / Daniel / Priya — quick technical readout based on the goals above. High-level feasibility and trade-offs: 

1) Quantized 13B support
- Redwood runtime supports int8/int4 quantized variants for many 13B families. We can run GGML-style quantized artifacts via our private deployment with an optimized kernel path. Expect ~1.6–2.2x token throughput improvement vs non-quantized depending on hardware.

2) Latency at 256–512 tokens (99th)
- Single-request tail latency depends on GPU type and batch policy. Example projections (on A100/80GB equiv):
  - Dedicated 1xA100: approx 120–280ms for 256 tokens at low batching; 256 tokens 99th ~320ms worst-case under shared traffic.
  - Multi-GPU sharded (2xA100): better headroom for 512 token tails, 99th ~260–340ms depending on KV cache locality.

3) Throughput and scaling
- For embeddings (200 QPS) we recommend a dedicated CPU+GPU pool with persistent cache nodes. Embedding models are cheaper; we can hit 200 QPS with a small cluster (2–3 mid-tier GPUs).
- For generation (40 QPS, mixed lengths) a target cluster of 2xA100 with continuous batching and session-aware KV cache should meet SLOs with autoscaling for bursts.

4) Graceful degradation strategy
- Automatic model-fallback: high-capacity endpoint routes to a smaller 7B model when capacity constrained. We can configure quality thresholds (BLEU/embedding-sim thresholds) and route based on SLO policy.

5) Security/compliance
- Private deployment supports customer-managed KMS, audit log forwarding to your SIEM, and SOC 2 artefacts (we can share report under NDA).

Open questions for sizing accuracy (Daniel/Priya):
- Sample p99 CPU/mem consumption per session (if available)
- Typical concurrency per user session (how many parallel calls per session)

I'll put together a 1–page topology diagram and two sizing options (conservative & cost-optimized) — will drop into the Drive link Neha shared by EOD tomorrow.

—Karthik
Staff Engineer, Inference Platforms
Redwood Inference
